A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Selective Aggregation research. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and can be matched despite reflow and table renumbering.

before.justification: v2 reports original classification experiments, attention analyses, aggregation ablations, and object-localization results in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those original experiments and adds classification benchmarks, cross-model aggregation-entropy results, and additional pooling-network ablations.

M1.justification: Section 5 retains the linear AbMILP scorer, softmax-weighted token aggregation, frozen encoder, and joint training of the aggregator and classifier. Expanded MLP ablations leave the adopted method unchanged.

E1.justification: Table 2 adds fine-grained recognition of cars, pets, and foods through Stanford Cars, OxfordIIIPets, and Food-101, plus multilabel classification on NUS-WIDE and COCO. This substantially broadens represented domains and task requirements while retaining ImageNet, ImageNet-1%, CUB, and localization coverage.

E2.justification: The C.2 comparison against the adopted linear aggregator adds GeLU MLP alternatives and three-/four-layer pooling variants. Existing standard pooling, non-trainable aggregation, and Attentive Probing comparators remain. SA-AbMILP and its 74.83% result remain in prose despite disappearing from the ablation table.

E3.justification: B.2 applies the existing LARS/batch-16,384 regime to Food-101, NUS-WIDE, and COCO, and SGD/batch-1,024 to Cars and Pets. Added analyses introduce across-block entropy summaries and deeper pooling-network configurations. Settings for retained benchmarks are unchanged; multilabel scoring is not clearly specified.

E4.justification: New Table 3 extends the aggregation-entropy diagnostic beyond MAE to other MIM models. C.2 expands the depth/activation ablation to test whether deeper MLPs improve pooling. Existing attention-flow, non-trainable aggregation, KLD, Attentive Probing, and localization analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions state in B.2 that results are averaged over three random seeds. Neither adds confidence intervals, dispersion estimates, significance tests, or a changed repeated-run procedure.

E6.justification: Table 2 adds substantial transfer and multilabel results while preserving its original scores. For example, new CAPI standard/selective scores are 45.6/76.8 on Cars and 72.3/80.1 on COCO; BEIT-v2 instead scores 93.7/93.4 on Pets. Tables 3 and 5 add entropy and ablation results. Retained ImageNet, Attentive Probing, and localization scores are unchanged; original ablation values are merely rounded.

T1.justification: The ViT and MAE definitions, Selective Aggregation equations, parameter-count reasoning, and normalized Shannon-entropy formula are retained. No theorem, proof, formal assumption, or substantive mathematical derivation is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims: MIM aggregation is insufficiently selective, and lightweight Selective Aggregation improves its global representations. Added experiments support the existing claims without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: C.1 adds an interpretation connecting the broader entropy results to diffuse aggregation across MIM models and explains I-JEPA/CAPI average pooling as uniform effective attention. The stated checkpoint-availability and generalization limitations, and the existing Attentive Probing interpretations, remain unchanged.

D1.justification: B.2 documents which optimizer and batch-size regimes apply to the five added datasets, and Table 5 specifies the additional pooling depths and activations. Acknowledgements newly identify PLGrid computing support. Reported code access and the four-GH200 hardware setup are unchanged.

R1.justification: v3 adds references for the five new datasets and removes the histological-representation reference previously cited for SA-AbMILP, using the already-cited kernel-self-attention work consistently. Sections 2 and A otherwise retain the same research positioning.

P1.justification: Section order and most prose are retained. v3 corrects typographical errors, updates author affiliations and appendix-reference wording, expands acknowledgements, and adds localized explanations accompanying the new experiments.

P2.justification: Table 2 expands from a single-column display to a full-width table; a new entropy table is inserted; and the ablation table becomes a depth-by-activation matrix. Figure 8 moves to a separate page and other material reflows, while the existing figure designs and plotted findings remain.

improvement.justification: Broader transfer and multilabel evaluation, direct entropy comparisons beyond MAE, and expanded pooling ablations strengthen the existing empirical argument and support the lightweight design. These are incremental gains over an already extensive evaluation. Unclear multilabel scoring and unchanged uncertainty reporting limit interpretation of some new results, particularly small differences, but the added evidence provides a clear overall benefit.
